answer: In an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded-length random walks from independently anchored identities, limiting how far endorsements can diffuse. A sybil cluster may resemble an oasis, grove, or reef internally, yet if few weighted edges cross its boundary, its low conductance creates a sparse cut. Min-cut and transitivity bounds then cap the probability mass—and thus voting weight—it can draw from honest anchors, preventing internal sybil volume from amplifying influence.
